knowledge:
- key_parameters: filter=An object of class filter, filterResult, or filterResultList specifying the gate(s) to plot ;; smooth=Logical; if TRUE, plots a smoothed 2D density representation with geometric gate outlines; if FALSE, plots individual events as points ;; xbin=Numeric; sets the bin size for hexbin scatter plots when smooth=FALSE to speed up rendering ;; stat=Logical; if TRUE, adds population statistics (e.g., percentage) to the plot ;; pos=Numeric; controls the label position of the statistics ;; abs=Logical; specifies whether the stat label position is absolute or relative to the filter boundary ;; outline=Logical; if TRUE in non-smoothed plots, draws the outline of the gate ;; channels=Character vector; specifies which channels to display in multi-panel density plots ;; par.settings=A named list of graphical parameters (e.g., gate, gate.density, gate.text, flow.symbol) to customize plot appearance ;; names=Logical or character vector; controls whether and how population names are displayed on the plot
- alternatives: lattice=The base visualization package upon which flowViz is built, which can be used for general plotting but lacks native flow cytometry gate rendering ;; flowCore=The core package used for data manipulation, transformation, and filtering before visualization
- when_to_use: Use flowViz when you need to visualize flow cytometry data (flowFrame or flowSet objects) and overlay geometric gates (e.g., rectangle, ellipsoid, polygon) or data-driven gates (e.g., norm2Filter, curv2Filter) to inspect populations.
- pitfalls: Avoid using complex R expressions in the formula interface as they can change the scale of raw data, making gate representations invalid ;; Computing data-driven filters (like curv2Filter) inside the plot call is computationally expensive; compute the filterResult once and pass it instead ;; Non-smoothed plots (smooth=FALSE) can be extremely slow for large datasets; use xbin (hexbin) or smoothed plots instead ;; Overplotting in non-smoothed scatter plots can hide underlying structure; partial transparency (alpha) can help but has scalability limits on some graphics devices

workflows.name: two_dimensional_scatter_plots
workflows.intent: Visualize flow cytometry data in 2D scatter plots with geometric or data-driven gates.
input: GvHD (flowSet object containing flow cytometry data)
workflows.stages: 1. Subset the flowSet to the patient of interest ;; 2. Transform fluorescence channels using asinh ;; 3. Define geometric gates (rectangleGate) or data-driven gates (norm2Filter, curv2Filter) ;; 4. Plot using xyplot with the filter argument (smoothed, non-smoothed, hexbin, or with statistics)
workflows.code:
GvHD <- GvHD[pData(GvHD)$Patient==6]
tf <- transformList(from=colnames(GvHD)[3:7], tfun=asinh)
GvHD <- tf %on% GvHD
rgate <- rectangleGate("FSC-H"=c(0, 400),"SSC-H"=c(-50, 300))
xyplot(`SSC-H` ~ `FSC-H` | Visit, data=GvHD, filter=rgate)
rgate2 <- rgate * rectangleGate("FL1-H"=c(2, 4))
xyplot(`SSC-H` ~ `FSC-H` | Visit, data=GvHD, filter=rgate2)
xyplot(`SSC-H` ~ `FSC-H` | Visit, data=GvHD, filter=rgate, smooth=FALSE)
xyplot(`SSC-H` ~ `FSC-H` | Visit, data=GvHD, filter=rgate, smooth=FALSE,xbin=128)
xyplot(`SSC-H` ~ `FSC-H` | Visit, data=GvHD, filter=rgate, smooth=FALSE, stat=TRUE,pos=0.5,abs=TRUE)
recGate1<-rectangleGate("FL4-H"=c(3.3,5.3),"FL2-H"=c(2.5,5))
recGate2<-rectangleGate("FL4-H"=c(4,6),"FL2-H"=c(6,8))
filters1<-filters(list(recGate1,recGate2))
xyplot(`FL2-H` ~ `FL4-H` ,data=GvHD[[1]] ,filter=filters1 ,stat=TRUE ,margin=FALSE )
n2Filter <- norm2Filter("SSC-H", "FSC-H", scale=2, filterId="Lymphocytes")
n2Filter.results <- filter(GvHD, n2Filter)
xyplot(`SSC-H` ~ `FSC-H` | Visit, data=GvHD, filter=n2Filter.results)
c2f <- curv2Filter("FSC-H", "FL4-H", bwFac=1.8)
c2f.results <- filter(GvHD, c2f)
xyplot(`FL4-H` ~ `FSC-H` | Visit, data=GvHD, filter=c2f.results)

workflows.name: one_dimensional_density_plots
workflows.intent: Visualize 1D kernel density estimates of flow cytometry channels with gate boundaries.
input: GvHD (flowSet object containing flow cytometry data)
workflows.stages: 1. Define 1D filters (e.g., curv1Filter) ;; 2. Plot single-channel density with gate boundaries using densityplot ;; 3. Plot multi-channel density with a list of filters using densityplot
workflows.code:
densityplot(~ `FSC-H`, GvHD, filter=curv1Filter("FSC-H"))
densityplot(~ ., GvHD, channels=c("FSC-H", "SSC-H", "FL1-H"), filter=list(curv1Filter("FSC-H"), NULL, rgate2))

workflows.name: parallel_coordinate_plots
workflows.intent: Visualize multi-dimensional flow cytometry data using parallel coordinate plots grouped by filter results.
input: GvHD (flowSet object containing flow cytometry data)
workflows.stages: 1. Compute filter results (e.g., norm2Filter) ;; 2. Plot using parallel with the filter argument
